patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact header with a small boxed logo on the left and a classic three-line menu icon on the right, implying a collapsed navigation that must open on tap.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the hamburger should reveal the site navigation, likely as an off-canvas panel or full-screen menu. It should also support closing via the same trigger, an explicit close control, or tapping outside if an overlay is used.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a drawer, dropdown, or full-screen takeover.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Because the mobile sketch includes a hamburger-triggered hidden navigation, opening that navigation implies keyboard focus must move into the revealed menu and return to the trigger when closed.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move to the first actionable item or close control; when it closes, focus should return to the hamburger button. If the menu behaves like an overlay/drawer, focus containment may be needed while open.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Depends on whether the opened menu is implemented as a simple disclosure panel or a modal-like overlay.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows a horizontal top navigation with multiple grouped labels and a large content area beneath that resembles category-driven navigation or submenu structure, suggesting expandable top-level nav items.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Desktop nav items may reveal submenus or mega menus on hover or click. If multiple categories are present, only one submenu may be open at a time, and keyboard access should mirror pointer behavior.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw open submenu panels under the nav, so this is inferred from the grouped nav layout rather than directly shown.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: If the desktop top navigation contains expandable submenu behavior, keyboard users will need managed focus through top-level items and revealed submenu links.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Focus should move logically through nav triggers and submenu items; if submenus open on focus/click, they should close predictably on blur, Escape, or moving away. Programmatic state updates may be needed for accessible disclosure behavior.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Only applicable if the desktop nav is implemented with interactive submenus rather than plain links.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven article page with relatively light JavaScript needs. The clearest required interaction is the mobile collapsed navigation via hamburger. Desktop appears to use a fuller horizontal navigation that may expose dropdown or mega-menu behavior, though that is somewhat inferred rather than explicitly drawn. No forms, tabs, accordions, modals, infinite loading, or toast-like feedback are visibly indicated in either viewport.
